The reference for an age from CPR numbers

Source: R/add_cpr_info.R
age_at.Rd

Use inside add_cpr_info() to say when the age is measured: alder = age_at(year). It describes the reference; the age is calculated by add_cpr_info(). For a vector of ages, see cpr_age().

Usage

age_at(ref, at = "primo")

Arguments

ref

The reference, as a value, a column of the data or an expression on its columns. Its type decides what it is:

  • whole numbers are years, and at chooses the day in the year;

  • a Date vector or ISO date strings ("YYYY-MM-DD") are dates.

One value for all rows, or one per row. Left out, the reference is today, Sys.Date().

at

The day in the year, when ref is a year:

  • "primo" (default): 31 December of the year before, the opening of the year. age_at(2025) is the age on 31 December 2024.

  • "jan1": 1 January.

  • "medio": 1 July.

  • "ultimo": 31 December.

Not allowed when ref is a date.

Value

An age specification for add_cpr_info().

Details

Why primo is the day before. In population statistics the opening population of a year is the closing population of the year before, and the ages must agree: age_at(year) equals age_at(year - 1, "ultimo"). A person born on 1 January 2000 is therefore 0 in age_at(2001). Use "jan1" to count that birthday, which gives 1. The choice moves the age reference only, not who is in the population.

Missing references give missing ages. A data column takes precedence over a variable of the same name where the function is called; .env$name and .data$name make the source explicit. A number is always a year: for a date held as a number, convert it with as.Date() first.

The name says what the argument is, the time the age is measured at. In daos the helper was age(year, at, date, primo). date is now the same argument as the year, and primo = "jan1" is the at value "jan1".

See also

add_cpr_info(), cpr_age()

Examples

df <- data.frame(pnr = "0101004007", year = 2025L,
                 seen = as.Date("2025-07-01"))
add_cpr_info(df, pnr, age_at(year), sex)
#>          pnr year       seen age sex
#> 1 0101004007 2025 2025-07-01  24   1
add_cpr_info(df, pnr,
  primo = age_at(year),
  jan1 = age_at(year, "jan1"),
  ultimo = age_at(year, "ultimo"))
#>          pnr year       seen primo jan1 ultimo
#> 1 0101004007 2025 2025-07-01    24   25     25
add_cpr_info(df, pnr, alder = age_at("2025-07-01"))
#>          pnr year       seen alder
#> 1 0101004007 2025 2025-07-01    25
add_cpr_info(df, pnr, alder = age_at(seen))
#>          pnr year       seen alder
#> 1 0101004007 2025 2025-07-01    25
